title: Implementing Functional Languages: a tutorial
byline: Simon L. Peyton Jones and David R. Lester · Prentice Hall, 1992 (free electronic edition)
note: PDF page = printed page + 1. Appendices (utilities module, example Core programs) and chapter conclusions are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A hands-on course in building implementations of lazy functional languages, written as runnable Miranda (easily read as Haskell). It defines a small Core language with a parser and pretty-printer, then builds a sequence of increasingly realistic evaluators, each in numbered “Marks”: a template-instantiation graph reducer, the G-machine (compiling supercombinators to stack code), the Three Instruction Machine (TIM, a spineless closure-based design), and a parallel G-machine. A final chapter covers the front-end transformations that feed them: lambda lifting, Johnsson-style lifting, full laziness and dependency analysis. Every machine is specified as a state transition system, which makes the designs easy to compare.
